title: Configuring DHCP Options for a Site

blocks.text: You can configure Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) options to provide additional network configuration parameters for devices that obtain IP addresses from the Zero Trust Branch appliance when the DHCP service is enabled while configuring a site. These options allow admins to automatically provide settings such as DNS servers, domain names, Network Basic Input/Output System (NetBIOS) information, or vendor-specific parameters to clients when they join the network.
To configure DHCP options for a site:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Deployments > Sites.
On the Sites page, click the site in the Site Name column for which you want to configure DHCP options.
On the site details page, click the Settings tab, then click DHCP Profile (Default).
In the DHCP Options section, click Add Option.
In the Add DHCP Options drawer:

DHCP Option: Select a DHCP option from the drop-down menu. You can choose a predefined DHCP option (e.g., Domain Server, Domain Name, or Vendor Specific) from the list or select Custom to define your own option.
The following table lists of supported DHCP options:

table: Specifies the DNS servers that DHCP clients use to resolve domain names.
Defines the domain name assigned to DHCP clients for hostname resolution.
Provides vendor-specific configuration parameters to supported devices.
Specifies the NetBIOS name servers that clients use for NetBIOS name resolution.
Identifies the NetBIOS datagram distribution server used for NetBIOS message distribution.
Defines the NetBIOS node type that determines how NetBIOS names are resolved.
Specifies the NetBIOS scope identifier that clients use for NetBIOS communication.
Specifies the duration of the DHCP lease assigned to clients.
Specifies the time when a DHCP client begins renewing its IP address lease.
Specifies the time when a DHCP client attempts to renew the IP address lease from any available DHCP server if renewal fails.
Identifies the vendor type of the DHCP client to enable device-specific configuration.
Specifies a unique identifier that the DHCP client uses to identify itself to the DHCP server.
Specifies the hostname or IP address of the server that clients use to retrieve configuration files.
Specifies the name of the boot file that clients use during network boot (PXE).
Identifies a group or class of DHCP clients to which specific DHCP options or policies are applied.
Specifies a list of domain suffixes that clients use when resolving hostnames.
Identifies vendor-specific client classes using enterprise identifiers.
Provides vendor-specific configuration data associated with the vendor class identifier.
Specifies the Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server used by devices to retrieve configuration files (commonly for VoIP phone provisioning).

blocks.item: Name: (Optional) Enter a name for the custom DHCP option. This field appears only if you choose Custom as the DHCP Option.
Code: This field auto-populates with the numeric DHCP option code associated with the selected option. Custom options require you to manually enter the option code.

Type: This field auto-populates with the data format for the option value associated with the selected option, such as byte, string, word, long, or IP address. Custom options require you to manually select the data format from the drop-down menu.
Value: Enter the value for the DHCP option. The value's format must match the selected type. For example, if the Type is IP-address, then the value must be an IP address.

Filter: (Optional) Select a filter parameter from the drop-down menu. The filter parameter allows DHCP options to apply to specific devices in the network based on attributes such as MAC address, DHCP client identifier, etc.
Filter Value: (Optional) Enter the value that must be used to filter devices to which the DHCP options are applied. This field appears only if you select an option for the Filter field.
